# Connection for custom Agents

> Integrate authentication, user confirmation and external Action access without receiving provider credentials.

## Choose authentication

All Direct clients use Streamable HTTP at `__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp`.

- Product-integrated "Connect Connection" button: use registered Agent Consumer PAT Binding below, as RehoboamAI does.
- Existing remote OAuth MCP client: use Authorization Code + PKCE and the SDK's browser login/token lifecycle. Discover configuration at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. Coordinate OAuth client registration with the Connection administrator; do not assume unrestricted dynamic registration. Validate state, redirect URI and resource according to the actual SDK/profile. OAuth is separate from PAT Binding's callback/claim protocol.
- Personal/manual client: sign in at [Access tokens](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/tokens), issue a Connection PAT and store it in backend Secret configuration. Generic PATs use the Portable PAT Consumer.

Token authentication, external account connection and Consumer Action consent are separate requirements. Company approval is required only when enabled for that Provider; existing and new Providers default to approval off. A token alone does not grant external account access.

## Browser entrance admission

On deployments with entrance protection, only interactive browser pages and Browser APIs use direct company OAuth before LDAP login. Connection derives the business Principal, roles, existing connections and grants only from LDAP; entrance and LDAP accounts need not match. This does not migrate accounts. User PAT Binding confirmation and OAuth authorize/login are browser interactions and may require both logins. MCP, metadata, DCR, token/refresh/revoke and PAT Binding backend create/claim retain their original credentials with no company admission cookie or extra apiKey. Never forward company identity headers as user credentials or follow a machine response into an HTML login flow. Browser entrance expiration requires the user to reopen the console and complete admission before explicitly retrying; do not automatically replay writes. Company admission lasts 30 minutes; Connection logout and company SSO logout are separate. The registered callback page automatically completes admission before LDAP login, with a manual “完成公司登录” fallback if automatic continuation is unavailable.

## Register an Agent Consumer and obtain its service credential

Developers and ordinary users must submit the Consumer ID, Agent name and fixed Callback URL to a Connection administrator for registration. The management page is administrator-only; ordinary users visiting it return to My Connection. Administrators use [Agent integration management (administrators only)](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/admin/agents).

Provide a stable `consumerId` (3-80 lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, beginning with a letter or digit), `consumerName` (1-100 characters) and fixed HTTPS `callbackUrl`, e.g. `https://agent.example/connection/callback`. The callback cannot contain username/password or a fragment and cannot be supplied or changed by a binding request. Registration validates the URL format without accessing or checking the existence of the callback endpoint. Implement the callback and ensure it is reachable from the user's browser before starting user binding.

Registration displays the service credential once. Deliver it securely and store it only in backend Secret configuration. This service credential authenticates binding create/claim calls; it is not the user PAT and cannot be used to call MCP. Ordinary users must contact the administrator rather than substitute a personal PAT.

Registration continues directly into capability configuration. The administrator selects Provider/Actions and saves the capability configuration. "Configure capabilities" later shows saved selections for review and editing. This is the upper bound of requestable capabilities; it does not grant an external account. If authorization reports missing client capabilities, ask the Connection administrator to configure that Provider for the Agent.

## Implement per-user PAT Binding

1. Authenticate the user in your product and associate each binding with the initiating user/session/instance in your backend. `principalHint` is optional: when available, derive it from that trusted user's company email; it must match the Connection browser account after trimming and lowercasing. When omitted, the user explicitly links the current Connection account, which may differ from the product account. Null, blank or invalid hints are rejected. Connection derives the Principal only from its own authenticated browser session.
2. From your backend, send:

```http
POST __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/api/v1/connection/pat-bindings
Authorization: Bearer <Agent service credential>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: <UUID for this create operation>

{"consumerId":"my-agent","name":"my-agent-default"}
```

The HTTP 201 response contains `bindingId`, `authorizationUrl`, `expiresAt`. Persist the binding ID association to the initiating product user/session/instance. Open the returned authorization URL in a new tab; do not construct it or trust caller-supplied identities.

3. The user signs in to Connection and sees the current Connection account, "Authorize <Agent name>", the token name and expiry, and the account information shared with the backend. Explicit confirmation creates an independent user/Consumer instance and PAT, then redirects with HTTP 303 to the registered callback, adding `binding_id=<bindingId>`. The callback URL never carries the PAT or account profile.
4. In your backend callback, verify the binding ID belongs to the initiating user/session/instance before claiming or attaching it. Do not attach an arbitrary callback ID to the currently logged-in user. Claim with the same Consumer's service credential:

```http
POST __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/api/v1/connection/pat-bindings/<bindingId>/claim
Authorization: Bearer <Agent service credential>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: <different UUID for this claim operation>

{"consumerId":"my-agent"}
```

The response is `{"issued":{"account":{"id":...,"email":...,"displayName":...},"consumerId":...,"expiresAt":...,"name":...,"token":...,"tokenId":...}}`. `account.id` is the stable Connection Principal identifier of this PAT; email is the current Connection profile email or null, not a stable identity key or evidence that product and Connection accounts belong to the same person. Encrypt/store `issued.token` for the initiating product user/instance in backend Secret configuration and record the token ID/expiry. The UI may show the linked account email/name; never expose the token to the frontend or models. Existing clients may continue providing principalHint and reading the original issued fields.

The binding currently lasts 10 minutes; both confirmation and claim must finish before the returned binding expiry. PAT expiry is separately returned in `issued.expiresAt`. Claim succeeds once. Use separate create/claim idempotency keys, preserving a key and parameters for the same operation; do not rely on replay to retrieve a one-time secret. Expired, delivered or lost-response cases require an explicit new binding flow rather than blind claim retries. Users can revoke an already issued obsolete token at [Access tokens](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/tokens).

## Provider approval setting, account connection and Consumer consent

Connection's HTML confirmation POST carries a short-lived session/account/binding/origin proof in a hidden field; the backend create/claim contract is unchanged. Missing or null Origin is accepted only with a valid proof and authenticated session; explicit foreign Origin is rejected. Do not proxy the page, construct confirmation requests, put proof or PAT in URLs, or bypass checks by user-agent. Confirmation proofs last at most five minutes and never beyond the binding expiry. After expiry, account/session change or a legacy page without proof, reopen the authorization link. Share the displayed error reference for troubleshooting, not headers, Cookie, proof, state or token. Real embedded-browser compatibility remains subject to client acceptance.

Company entry completion, native LDAP OAuth login and administrator identity probes use separate contextual browser proofs. Console JSON mutations send their anonymous short-lived proof in a header; the proof never grants identity or permissions. Missing/isolated cookies require fresh authentication and confirmation, optionally in the system browser through the displayed recovery link. Recovery reconstructs only a safe original GET page and never retries POSTs. URLs never carry passwords, PATs or confirmation proofs. Machine endpoints and Provider OAuth state/PKCE contracts remain unchanged.

Enabling approval also blocks new calls from existing directly connected accounts without valid company eligibility. Disabling approval preserves history, does not expand Credential scopes or selected Actions, and does not automatically restore suspended or revoked Consumer grants. Shared-account eligibility is managed separately.

Binding confirmation issues a token that can use connections already granted to that Consumer; it does not create an account connection, company approval or Action grant.

1. At [Connections](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections), select a Provider and follow its current approval setting. Approval is off by default: connect your own external account directly. Only when an administrator enables approval, select "Request connection", supply purpose, select capabilities and acknowledge the disclaimer before submitting a company approval request.
2. At [My Connection](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections), users select a Provider to inspect their connection requests. For Providers with approval enabled, assigned approvers use [Awaiting my approval](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/approvals). Users cannot approve on their own behalf; PAT issuance does not bypass enabled approval.
3. With approval off, connect directly. With approval on, obtain approval first. Return to Connections and select an existing account or connect an external account. Reapplication, renewal and new capability approval apply to Providers with approval enabled and start from the account's available operations.
4. Select the account, choose "Authorize client", select the Agent Consumer and explicitly confirm the Actions.

If the Agent/Action is not selectable, ask the administrator to check registration, enabled state and Declaration. Do not substitute another Consumer's token. A user PAT can use multiple Providers explicitly granted to that Consumer. Token revocation, grant revocation and disconnecting an account have different scopes.

## Configure MCP and discover Actions

Have the backend MCP transport read the current user/instance PAT from Secret storage:

```text
Transport: Streamable HTTP
URL: __CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/mcp
Authorization: Bearer <Connection PAT>
```

These are protocol parameters, not a complete SDK configuration. Validate compatibility for the actual SDK/version; Codex conformance does not prove compatibility for another client.

After initialization, call `tools/list` and use the five generic tools:

1. `list_apps`: discover providers.
2. `list_connections`: inspect available accounts.
3. `search_actions`: find an Action; when the Provider is known, use the actual schema's `service` filter to receive missing-connection/authorization guidance.
4. `get_action_guide`: read the input schema, permissions and idempotency requirements.
5. `execute_action`: execute with the actual schema/guide.

`AUTHORIZED` is not an execution receipt and does not prove a write was never submitted. Preserve the original idempotency key when checking/retrying the same operation. A deterministic Provider rejection is `FAILED`; a transport or terminal-persistence failure remains unknown (`PROVIDER_UNCERTAIN` / `UNCERTAIN`). Do not switch keys or reauthorize just because execution is pending or rejected.

Do not guess Action IDs or submit raw provider credentials or caller-supplied user/Consumer/Agent identities. Keep service credentials and user PATs separate. Neither may enter model input, chat, frontend storage, source, logs or URLs. Never share one PAT across users; independent instances require separate tokens for independent audit/revocation.

## Permission recovery and current error coverage

For `list_connections`/`search_actions` empty results with `service`, inspect `result.structuredContent.guidance`: `message`, `messageKey`, `reasonCode`, `retryable`, `nextAction`. `nextAction.type=OPEN_CONNECTION_WEB` includes a URL such as `__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections?provider=jira&intent=authorize`.

- `PROVIDER_NOT_CONNECTED`: open Connections and connect according to the current setting; request approval first only for a Provider with approval enabled.
- `PROVIDER_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED`: select the account and authorize this client; complete missing company approval first only if that Provider has approval enabled and select the Provider in My Connection to inspect request progress.
- `PROVIDER_REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED`: inspect the account's state and reconnect or reconfirm client consent as directed; check and restore company eligibility only if that Provider has approval enabled.
- `PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED` / `CONTACT_ADMIN`: ask the Connection administrator to admit the Provider; do not imply the user simply needs to grant it.
- `SEARCH_NO_RESULTS` / `REFINE_SEARCH`: simplify the query; empty results do not necessarily mean missing permission.
- HTTP 401/token expiry: repeat client login or PAT Binding; manual PAT users should inspect Access tokens for expiry/revocation.

Current discovery guidance does not distinguish every company approval state. Execution errors do not all carry `nextAction.url`; do not assume a universal error envelope or URL field. For generic `FORBIDDEN` or permission failures without links, show the safe server message and offer [My Connection (accounts and requests)](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/connections) and [Help](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/help) so the user can inspect account, approval and client grants. Do not assert a particular approval state or automatically submit/approve requests.

Only show validated Connection-site URLs as action links. Open navigation in a new tab, preserving the Agent session. Wait for user action when `retryable=false`. Do not replay a business WRITE with an unknown outcome after restoring authorization.

## Delegated Agent platforms

Per-user PAT Binding remains Direct MCP access. A platform representing the current Principal through a registered workload must coordinate the HTTP/OpenAPI Delegated contract, workload identity and short-lived delegated context with the administrator. Agent Platform requires a stable registered Agent Actor. Do not replace this contract with caller-supplied identities/shared PATs or infer Delegated endpoints from the MCP URL.

## Public guide

[Developer integration guide](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/agent/)

Open guide/console links in new tabs. Do not infer undocumented endpoints, credentials, identities or grants from this file.

## Newly published capabilities

New capabilities require explicit Consumer consent. Candidates are bounded by the published catalog, Consumer declaration and company approval, not the saved external scope snapshot. Consent permits client use; the Provider determines actual operation permissions. Scope changes do not pause grants. Permission failures affect the operation only; recovery does not require repeat Consumer consent. Genuine credential expiry or revocation still requires reconnect. Healthy accounts have no persistent permission-refresh button. Only server-indicated upgrade or reconnect states expose recovery actions; new Actions or external scope changes do not require account updates. New-capability notices exclude old unchecked catalog Actions. Never collect credentials in chat or silently grant new Actions.

## Rehoboam release failure handoff

Before final delivery or reissuing Iris, READ `get_release_family_continuation`. It returns remaining confirmation/delivery steps, a version suggestion from the live template separator/step and affected downstream tasks. Use existing preview/confirm replacement and initialize the new member; preserve Native, old versions and requests. Explicitly select new upstream results, not old bound URLs. A suggestion is not a reservation; final delivery requires the existing confirmed notice flow and receipt readback.

Do not require users to declare a local checkout or assume source repair authority. Diagnose first, hand source changes to project developers unless explicitly requested. All release-family stages (Jobs, manual PR, tests/results, decisions and delivery) support explicitly authorized Provider v14 `record_release_family_repair` with current revision/template signature. Generic resolved handling requires validation evidence; compilation still needs PR/full commit/CI. This is operator-reported progress, not task completion. Show ready-for-verification Job results and remaining confirmation/delivery steps and ask whether to continue. Do not advance, change Job outcomes, send messages, merge or build packages through handoff recording. Confirm business writes; read back uncertain outcomes before retrying.

## GitHub Actions Job logs

When the current catalog exposes `github.get_workflow_job_logs`, it requires separate explicit Consumer consent. Discover it and read its guide before calling; obtain the Job ID through `github.list_workflow_run_jobs`. Follow `nextStartLine` for another page. A truncated response is not the full log; when `scanLimitReached` is true and `nextStartLine` is null, direct the user to the GitHub Actions log. Reading never reruns a build. Raw build logs may enter the authorized consumer/model context; authorize only appropriate logs. See [GitHub help](__CONNECTION_ORIGIN__/connection/help?chapter=15) for defaults, limits and recovery.
